---
title: "Updating a summary"
---

Summaries change when new research is published, when a reviewer asks for changes, or when you spot a mistake.
All changes are made in Airtable, in the same tables you use to [add a summary](adding-a-summary.qmd).

## Editing a published summary

Changes to a *Preliminary* or *Reviewed* summary go live at the next sync run, which is overnight or whenever anyone presses Publish.

- **Half-finished edits can go live.**
  If your edits are valid when the overnight run happens, they are published, even if you haven't finished.
  For a big rewrite, prepare the new text and ratings elsewhere first (e.g. in a Word document or your rating table), then enter them in one sitting.
- **Mistakes don't take the page down.**
  If an edit leaves the summary invalid (e.g. a required field is blank), the last good version stays live and the summary shows *Needs fixing* until you fix it.
- **Never change the Slug** of a published summary.
  It is the page's web address, and old links would stop working.

## Small corrections

For typos, wording and broken links, edit the field and publish.
Don't change **Last reviewed**: it records when the *ratings* were last checked, not when the text was last touched.

## Adding new evidence

When a new meta-analysis or umbrella review covers an exposure:

1. **Add the reference.**
   Search the References table first; if it isn't there, add it.
   Link it to the summary, then drag it into alphabetical order in the summary's References field.
2. **Update the findings.**
   - If it reports an outcome the summary already has, update that row's Evidence detail, and re-rate it with [the rubric](rating-the-evidence.qmd).
     Agreement between independent meta-analyses can raise the evidence quality.
   - If it reports a new outcome, add a Findings row.
   - If it shows the effect differs by a factor, add or update a How effects differ row.
3. **Check the recommendations** still follow from the findings.
   Update or remove any Why this works that no longer holds.
4. **Update the evidence statistics** (Meta-analyses, Primary studies, Participants) and **About the evidence**.
5. **Review the overall rating** and the **Short summary** in the light of the new findings.
6. **Set Last reviewed** to today's date.
7. **Set Status back to *Preliminary*** if the summary was *Reviewed*, so the review team checks the changes.
   Let them know it's ready.
8. Run the [checklist before publishing](writing-guide.qmd#checklist-before-publishing), then publish.

## Removing something

- **A finding, How effects differ row or recommendation** belongs to one summary only, so you can delete the row.
- **A reference** may be shared with other summaries.
  **Unlink** it from this summary instead of deleting the row; deleting it removes it from every summary that cites it.

## Taking a summary off the website

Set its **Status** to *Draft*.
It is removed from the website at the next sync run, and nothing in Airtable is lost.
Check with the platform maintainer first, and don't delete the summary's row.

Take summaries off one or two at a time.
A run that would remove more than a fifth of the pages at once stops without publishing anything (see [When a whole run stops](publishing.qmd#when-a-whole-run-stops)).

## Undoing a change

Airtable keeps a revision history for each row: expand the row and look at its activity.
On the current plan this goes back two weeks.

## Bigger changes

Talk to the platform maintainer and the review team before you:

- merge two summaries, or split one;
- need a new exposure type, outcome domain or moderator in a dropdown;
- want a field that doesn't exist yet.

These change the structure of the base or the platform's code.
When the structure changes, the maintainer rebuilds the Airtable base and will ask everyone to **pause editing** for a while.
Before a rebuild, publish any changes you have made to a published summary and check its Sync status says *Published*.
The rebuild starts from the published version, so unpublished edits to it would be left behind.
Drafts are copied across.
After a rebuild the tables are new copies: Airtable comments and revision history stay with the old tables, which are kept for a while as a safety net.
